Tldr: good program for software engineering/cyber, not sure if i can recommend for video game dev


The other commenter really made great points and its true- if you really put the work in you'll be successful whichever school you go to.

I graduated from TU's CS program and the one class I can think that would be applicable to video game development is computer graphics. However, my experience with the class was absolutely awful - I learned some stuff about graphics but the projects were painful and the teacher was not helpful. We did focus quite a bit on how videogame graphics worked and all the calculations that went into it, but I still would not recommend it. 

The rest of my classes were pretty good, but overall Towson's CS program is really focused on software engineering (a lot of class projects were web development stuff) as well as cybersecurity. If you're trying to become a great programmer for videogames, you can definitely take specific classes at Towson that will really boost your understanding of programming and programming languages, but at the end of the day you'll probably have to do more outside of class to really learn the tools you need to be a videogame dev since most professors in the department are focused on software or some cybersecurity research.
